title: PineGate POC weekly - retention, SSO & SOC2 checkpoint
summary: Weekly POC sync focusing on security/compliance items: SSO integration progress, audit log ingestion and retention configuration, SOC2 evidence collection, and a short review of early inference results. Agree to run a short log export test and share SOC2 scoping doc by next Tue.
next_steps: Redwood to send SOC2 scoping checklist and map of where evidence lives - due 2026-03-10
Customer to run audit log export test and confirm format - due 2026-03-09
Schedule dedicated SSO test window with PineGate SSO admin - propose 2026-03-11
SE to provide small perf snapshot from dedicated worker config - due 2026-03-08
action_items: Samir Patel - produce log export sample and example ingestion script - 2026-03-09
Jamie Ortega - send SOC2 scoping doc and contact for compliance packet - 2026-03-10
Chris Yu - enable debug-level audit logs for 2h test window and share endpoint - 2026-03-09
Lena Morris - confirm acceptable retention windows and regulatory constraints (GDPR subset) - 2026-03-10
header: Meeting header: 2026-03-05 15:00 UTC | Duration: 46 mins | Attendees: Jamie Ortega (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Rina Cho (Redwood CSM), Lena Morris (PineGate Head of Security), Chris Yu (PineGate SRE), Dana Park (PineGate PM), Marco Silva (PineGate Procurement)
transcript:
[00:00] Jamie Ortega: Okay, thanks everyone for joining, well give it a minute for folks to pop in. uh quick intro from our side, Jamie here AE, Samir is our SE, Rina is on CSM.
[00:18] Lena Morris: Hey Jamie, thanks. Were running a little late but ready to go, here's Lena.
[00:22] Chris Yu: Chris, SRE, morning.
[00:25] Jamie Ortega: Great. Agenda for today: SSO status, audit logs and retention question, SOC2 evidence handoff, and a quick results snapshot. Any additions?
[00:35] Dana Park: No additions, maybe touch on perf cost briefly.
[00:38] Jamie Ortega: Yep, we will. Samir, do you want to kick off SSO?
[00:42] Samir Patel: Sure. So status: we completed the SAML metadata exchange last week, PineGate side configured the IdP and we pushed the SP metadata into your tenant. We did see one mismatch on NameID format, which was causing failed assertions, thats fixed now. SCIM provisioning - we still need a couple attributes mapped for groups.
[01:05] Lena Morris: That aligns with what we saw. Our SCIM schema is customized for department codes, so we need a mapping example.
[01:12] Samir Patel: Got it. Ill send a mapping sample; can do a mapping that adds a department claim in SCIM 2.0. Also to confirm: are you planning to use SSO for admin users only initially or for all users in the pilot?
[01:26] Dana Park: Admins only for the pilot, we want to keep control of who can spin up models.
[01:30] Jamie Ortega: Makes sense. From Redwood's side we'll treat that as RBAC with admin role bound to SAML group. We can also support SCIM-group to RBAC sync.
[01:40] Lena Morris: Okay next on audit logs. We received the sample endpoint you set up last week but the format didn't include request payloads, only top-level event types. We need full request/response pairs for traceability.
[01:53] Samir Patel: Right, current runtime emits structured events but payload masking is on by default. We can toggle debug-level logging for a short window to capture request bodies, but we want to make sure customer consents because that captures sensitive content.
[02:09] Chris Yu: We can do an ephemeral window. We'll set up a buffer rule and only run it for two hours, but we need the export format to be JSONL and include timestamps in ISO with nanoseconds if possible.
[02:21] Samir Patel: JSONL is fine. The runtime stores audit events in our managed audit pipeline for hosted customers, but for the PineGate pilot we suggested a forward to your AWS Kinesis Firehose. That still works?
[02:33] Chris Yu: Yes Kinesis is fine. We'll provide a temporary stream and credentials.
[02:38] Jamie Ortega: Important note: for Private deployments we can ship audit logs directly to a customer-controlled S3, if you switch to Private later you get more direct custody.
[02:48] Lena Morris: We're evaluating that, but for pilot Kinesis -> S3 is our preference. Next, retention. What are the default retention windows for hosted audit logs and for inference artifacts?
[03:00] Samir Patel: Default for hosted audit logs is 90 days. Inference artifacts (prompt/response KV cache fragments) are retained for 14 days by default with options to shorten. We can configure for longer if you need. For SOC2 you might need 1 year of certain records, so we can configure long-term export to Glacier as well.
[03:20] Lena Morris: For our compliance team, we need 12 months for auth events and 24 months for admin change history. Is that feasible?
[03:29] Samir Patel: Yes, we can configure tiered retention: keep auth events 12 months, admin change history 24 months, export to your S3 bucket then lifecycle to Glacier. We'll need to document the retention policy in the SOC2 mapping.
[03:41] Marco Silva: Quick procurement question - does extended retention impact pricing materially?
[03:45] Jamie Ortega: There is a storage cost; we can provide a conservative estimate. In general the incremental cost is small relative to per-token inference costs, but long-term cold storage has a minimal monthly fee. I will include an estimate in the pricing note.
[03:58] Dana Park: Great. SOC2 - Lena, do you have a list of specific evidence items you still need from us?
[04:03] Lena Morris: We have a checklist but we need clarity on where to find change logs for model deployments, tenant-level access logs, and any key rotation logs for KMS usage.
[04:12] Samir Patel: For model deployment change logs, those are recorded in our control plane audit stream and forwarded to the same audit pipeline. Tenant-level access logs are part of the auth events. KMS key rotation is logged in both Redwood's operational logs and in the KMS audit trail; for hosted customers we can surface a consolidated export.
[04:28] Jamie Ortega: I'll attach a mapping doc that shows which log type corresponds to which SOC2 control. That should make it easier for you to pull evidence.
[04:35] Lena Morris: Perfect. A couple of nitty gritty items: encryption in transit and at rest - we need confirmation that customer data is encrypted with customer-managed keys for Private, and for hosted that BYOK via KMS is supported.
[04:48] Samir Patel: Yes, hosted supports Bring Your Own Key (BYOK) via AWS KMS for customers who want it. For Private deployments you can run with your HSM/KMS. In both cases we rotate keys per your policy; rotation events are part of the audit stream.
[05:03] Chris Yu: On RBAC - can we get more granular roles beyond admin/read-only, like model-deploy-only or cost-view-only?
[05:09] Samir Patel: Yes, we have a role matrix. We can create custom roles that map to specific console and API permissions. I'll share the role matrix with examples.
[05:18] Jamie Ortega: Switching gears to a brief results review — Samir do you want to summarize the early inference metrics?
[05:23] Samir Patel: Sure. Over the last 48 hours the pilot ran about 8k requests, median latency 140ms for short prompts (~128 tokens predicted), p95 420ms. Cost per 1k tokens is trending lower than our initial hosted estimate because caching hit rate is about 28% for repeated prefixes.
[05:43] Dana Park: That latency is good, were mostly concerned about p95 spikes during batch windows.
[05:48] Samir Patel: Right the p95 spikes correlated with a nightly batch job that saturated the worker pool; we recommend an autoscale policy tweak to reserve capacity for interactive traffic. We can also set a routing policy so interactive goes to dedicated low-latency nodes.
[06:03] Chris Yu: Is that an additional charge to reserve capacity?
[06:06] Jamie Ortega: If you want guaranteed reserved capacity it's part of Dedicated offering, but we can set soft reservations with minimal cost impact for the pilot. We'll capture the options in the note.
[06:16] Lena Morris: Back to SSO test: Marco, do you have availability to run the provisioning test this week?
[06:22] Marco Silva: I can carve out time Friday morning, but need clear steps for the mapping and creds.
[06:27] Samir Patel: I'll email a step-by-step SCIM mapping doc and a checklist for Friday. Also include a small Python script for provisioning so you can run it locally.
[06:36] Lena Morris: Good. One more security ask: we need to validate that audit logs cannot be altered after ingestion. Can you describe immutability guarantees?
[06:45] Samir Patel: For hosted audit streams we maintain a write-once pipeline with SHA256 signatures appended and object versioning enabled on S3; you can also enable WORM policies on your bucket. For Private, you control the storage, so immutability is enforced by your S3/WORM/HSM settings.
[07:03] Chris Yu: Will those signatures include the full payload hash?
[07:07] Samir Patel: Yes, full payload hash; we keep a separate integrity index that you can query. That index can be included in the exported evidence.
[07:16] Dana Park: Any blockers on our side for SOC2 timeline? Were aiming for readiness review in late April.
[07:22] Lena Morris: We need the mapping doc and evidence locations this week, plus a successful SSO and log export test to close a few controls.
[07:31] Jamie Ortega: We'll prioritize the mapping doc. Rina will coordinate follow-ups and the SOC2 packet. Rina?
[07:35] Rina Cho: Yep Ill own the packet and will schedule a short working session next Tue to walk through the mapping with Lena and Chris.
[07:44] Marco Silva: Procurement question: once we confirm security and retention, whats the next contractual step?
[07:49] Jamie Ortega: Typically we move to a pilot amendment that captures retention SLAs and any privacy addendum; I'll draft and share a redline.
[07:57] Chris Yu: Quick note on audit log export test — we'll need a sample of redwoods JSONL schema to validate our parsers.
[08:03] Samir Patel: I'll attach the JSONL schema and an example file to the follow-up email.
[08:08] Dana Park: For the perf snapshot, can we see the dedicated worker config your SE suggested? We want to understand CPU/GPU allocation.
[08:15] Samir Patel: Yes, the config is small: worker type g4dn.xlarge for pilot, 16 concurrent processes, batch size guidance 8-16 depending on latency SLO. I'll put the exact YAML in the doc.
[08:29] [crosstalk] Lena Morris: sorry, go ahead.
[08:31] Samir Patel: Also note quantization profile used for the model is int8 with a small quality delta; we can run quality regression tests if you want.
[08:40] Dana Park: Please run that and show us delta on responses for our test prompts.
[08:45] Samir Patel: Will do.
[08:47] Jamie Ortega: Any regulatory residency questions?
[08:49] Lena Morris: For now EU residency for customer EU tenants — we need logs and data to stay in eu-west-1.
[08:55] Samir Patel: We can route regionally; for hosted we'll ensure data plane for EU tenants stays in eu-west-1, control plane remains global but with minimal PII. We'll document that architecture.
[09:09] Marco Silva: On pricing again - can you give a rough delta between enabling BYOK and standard managed keys?
[09:15] Jamie Ortega: BYOK has a minor setup fee and some additional monthly KMS charges, mostly driven by encryption API calls. I'll include a line-item estimate.
[09:26] Lena Morris: Okay lets recap next steps and owners.
[09:29] Jamie Ortega: Recap: Samir attach JSONL schema and provisioning script; Jamie send SOC2 mapping and pricing note; Rina schedule working session next Tue; Chris run audit log export test and share endpoint; Marco confirm availability Friday for SCIM run. Everyone in agreement?
[09:50] Chris Yu: Agree.
[09:51] Lena Morris: Agree.
[09:53] Dana Park: Agree.
[09:54] Jamie Ortega: Great, we'll follow up in email. Thanks all.
[09:58] [meeting end]
questions: How will audit logs include full request/response payloads without exposing sensitive data?
What retention windows are configurable and how do they map to SOC2 controls?
Does Redwood support BYOK and KMS key rotation logs for hosted customers?
notes: Redwood will support short-term debug-level logging for an ephemeral window but requires customer consent because of sensitive payloads.
Tiered retention and export to customer S3 recommended for SOC2 evidence.
SE to provide worker YAML and quantization impact tests.
